summary: [standards] The blob race of `artifacts move --commit` answers ARTIFACTS_STORE_UNAVAILABLE (exit 2, retryable true) after work was done, and the same invocation unchanged cannot pass. Driven with real calls: 4000 local blobs, preview, then `--commit --plan-digest D` while another process overwrote the head of 50 blobs once 200 objects were in the store, and put the bytes back after canon exited. First run: exit 2 ARTIFACTS_STORE_UNAVAILABLE retryable true, 3950 objects already uploaded. Second run, same command unchanged: PLAN_STALE (exit 2, retryable false), because the uploads turned the plan's `upload` effects into `skip`. ATIP 7.1.1: retryable means the same invocation unchanged can succeed; a failure after the work started is FAILED/INCOMPLETE (issue #135 (a) made this point for ARTIFACTS_STORE_FAILED, and this change does the opposite on the next branch). The registry meaning of ARTIFACTS_STORE_UNAVAILABLE ('before any blob was written ... nothing was written') and the CHANGELOG ('run the command again once the other process is done') are false for this path. Cause: artifacts.rs:553-556 pushes the code inside the commit loop after `uploaded` > 0; before this change it was ARTIFACTS_BLOB_CORRUPT, not retryable. The branch has no test. Fix: when anything uploaded, answer the exit-1 ARTIFACTS_STORE_FAILED (uploads kept, no local blob removed, say so), else a non-retryable code; test a blob rewritten between the plan and the upload. Blast radius: the next branch (an object already in the store that does not verify -> ARTIFACTS_BLOB_CORRUPT) and the final `refuse(...)` are also exit-2 refusals after uploads.
